agency.name: South Dakota Department of Labor and Regulation, Division of Labor and Management (Workers' Compensation)

ttd.rateText: Sixty-six and two-thirds percent of the employee's earnings, not more than 100% of the state average weekly wage (rounded up to the next dollar) and not less than one-half of that amount (SDCL 62-4-3).
ttd.minText: If the employee earned less than 50% of the maximum, compensation may not exceed 100% of the employee's earnings after federal/state taxes and FICA (SDCL 62-4-3).

waiting.text: No temporary disability benefits are paid for an injury that does not incapacitate the employee for seven consecutive days; if the seven-day waiting period is met, benefits are computed from the date of injury (SDCL 62-4-2).

ttdDuration.text: SDCL 62-4-3 sets no maximum number of weeks for temporary total disability.

ppd.text: Permanent partial disability is paid at the TTD rate (subject to the § 62-4-3 limits) for a scheduled number of weeks per body part (e.g. thumb 50 weeks, index finger 35 weeks); injuries to the back or to unlisted body parts are paid as that percentage of 312 weeks that the impairment bears to the body as a whole (SDCL 62-4-6).

facts.text: The employee makes the initial selection of a medical practitioner or surgeon from among all licensed practitioners in the state and must notify the employer (SDCL 62-4-43).
Permanent total disability benefits receive a cost-of-living allowance each July 1: a 2.5% increase took effect on July 1, 2026.

The minimum and maximum are reset every July 1 from the state average weekly wage computed by the Department of Labor and Regulation (SDCL 62-4-3.1); for July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026 they were $554 (minimum) and $1,108 (maximum).
Mileage for travel to and from treatment is reimbursed at $0.76 per mile from October 1, 2026.
